title: Contraction Not Used with Accented Letter

illustrates.quote: Foreign language words or phrases within an English language paragraph are contracted. Use modified letter indicators to represent accented letters. If a modification applies to a letter that would be part of a contraction, do not use the contraction. Use UEB symbols for inverted punctuation.

blocks.text: The word wooded in Spanish is leñera.
blocks.features: Single sentence; the foreign (Spanish) word 'leñera' (with accented/modified letter ñ) is italicised in the print original.

braille.notes: One line, verbatim, no line number shown. Because the accented letter n-with-tilde falls where the 'er' contraction would otherwise span it (le-ñ-era), the contraction is NOT used around it: the word is spelled 'le^]n]a' with the accent-modifier letter indicator on the n and ordinary letters either side, per the second and third sentences of 1.16.3.

resolution: Both runs agree on wording; same F-68 rationale as example-1-18.
